decisive_items: A 7-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of progressive eruption of papules and nodules all over his body.
Dense diffuse cellular infiltrate composed mainly of foamy histiocytic cells and multinucleated Touton cells mixed with lymphocytes and eosinophils.
No clinical evidence of internal involvement was found on ultrasonography, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging results.
response.rationale: Juvenile xanthogranuloma is the classic pediatric non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis with yellow-red papules, Touton cells, and CD68+/S100- staining. The absence of internal involvement and the patient's age strongly favor JXG over necrobiotic xanthogranuloma (typically adult, periorbital) and Erdheim-Chester disease (systemic, bone involvement).

rejected.why: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma usually occurs in older adults with periorbital lesions and necrobiosis; the pediatric presentation and lack of necrobiosis are atypical.
Erdheim-Chester disease is a systemic histiocytosis with frequent internal organ and bone involvement, which is explicitly absent here.
